title.zh: 地圖上的帝國幻術：俄羅斯地理教科書如何編造「自古以來的神聖領土」
title.en: Cartographies of Empire: How Russian Textbooks Fabricate an Eternal "Geo-Body"

summary.zh:
【總結】俄羅斯前國防部長紹伊古曾直言「地理不是歷史，不容不同觀點」。這篇刊登於《政治地理學》（Political Geography）的前沿研究揭示了克里姆林宮如何將地理教育轉化為新帝國治理的隱蔽戰略工具。作者索菲亞·加夫里洛娃（Sofia Gavrilova）透過剖析俄羅斯中學地理教科書，揭示出一套精心建構的「空間連續性」（spatial continuity）話語機制：官方教育將沙皇俄國、蘇聯與當代俄羅斯聯邦強行熔鑄成一個超越時空、永恆存在的「超國家元身體」（transhistorical meta-state）。地理學在此不再客觀記錄地緣邊界的消長變遷，而是致力於否認斷裂，將侵略擴張洗白為自然的有機生長，並將克里米亞與烏克蘭東部四州合理化為俄羅斯不可分割的「歷史土地」。這項研究突破性地指出，威權政權的領土野心不僅仰賴地緣政治宣傳，更取決於學校日常知識生產對帝國鄉愁的內化。

【研究問題】長期以來，關於威權宣傳與愛國主義教育的研究多聚焦於歷史學科的竄改，或停留在國家菁英的地緣政治論述層面，卻忽視了看似中立客觀的「地理教育」。在常人眼中，地形、氣候與地圖屬於自然科學範疇，這種對學科客觀性的迷信，恰恰使地理教育成為最危險的意識形態容器。過去學界缺乏對地理教育基礎設施、出版機制與視覺話語技術的微觀解構。本研究旨在回答兩個關鍵問題：當代俄羅斯教科書呈現了何種國家地理想像？普丁政權與其欽點的「文明企業家」俄羅斯地理學會（RGS），究竟透過何種話語與製圖技術，在學校課堂中確立國家的「地理身體」（geo-body）及其內部階層秩序？

【研究方法】研究採用批判地緣政治、話語分析與後殖民空間理論，以紮根理論（Grounded Theory）質性解讀俄羅斯教育部指定、俄羅斯地理學會審定的8至9年級核心地理教科書《北極星》（Poliarnaya Zvezda）系列（涵蓋烏克蘭全面戰爭爆發前後的2021至2024年各版本）及官方地圖集。作者跳脫傳統文本分析的僵化框架，細緻剖析其敘事修辭、地圖圖層疊加與視覺排版策略，著重檢視教科書如何將泰國學者通猜（Winichakul）所稱的「國家地理身體」加以神聖化，並追蹤其如何將領土掠奪「去殖民化」與「去政治化」。

【結果】研究發現，教科書透過三層精密的空間技術重塑現實：第一是「語意漂白」，全書數百頁中「殖民」一詞僅出現兩次，其餘征服皆被「開墾」、「遷徙」、「自然推進」等生態演化辭彙取代；2023與2024年版更迅速將烏克蘭被佔領區無縫編入「南部大區」，以「具有過渡制度的地戰略領土」入圖，並以醒目引言宣告「2014年開啟了收復歷史土地的進程」。第二是「內部東方主義」的等級化構造：莫斯科被定調為天賦動態進取心的「文明核心」，而西伯利亞與遠東等少數民族邊陲則被描繪為氣候惡劣、被動落後且僅供榨取資源的「未開化自然」，教科書甚至刻意將聯合國教科文組織的「文化遺產」全部分配在歐洲俄羅斯，亞洲部分則僅標註「自然遺產」。這些發現證明，空間連續性是當代威權政權編造領土合法性的核心手段，將擴張主義包裝成不可抗拒的歷史宿命。
summary.en:
**Summary:** When Russia's then-Defence Minister Sergei Shoigu proclaimed that "there should be no difference of opinion on geography—it is not history," he heralded a pedagogical turn that transformed school cartography into an instrument of neo-imperial statecraft. In this illuminating study published in *Political Geography*, Sofia Gavrilova investigates how contemporary Russian geography textbooks (2021–2024) systematically construct an illusion of "spatial continuity." By flattening the Russian Empire, the Soviet Union, and the post-Soviet federation into a singular, transhistorical "meta-state," state geography actively erases historical ruptures and naturalizes territorial revanchism. Contested borderlands like Crimea and the Donbas are reimagined as an organic part of an eternal Russian geo-body, positioning conquest not as violent transgression, but as the inevitable recovery of historical inheritance.

**Problem:** While scholars have thoroughly dissected Vladimir Putin’s revision of history textbooks and elite geopolitical rhetoric, critical geography has surprisingly overlooked the pedagogical production of territoriality within school curricula. Geography is popularly regarded as a technical, objective description of the physical earth; this perceived neutrality makes it an exceptionally powerful ideological vehicle. Previous research left a major analytical gap: How does an authoritarian regime utilize the epistemic infrastructures of everyday geographical education—institutionalized through the state-backed Russian Geographical Society (RGS)—to manufacture territorial legitimacy, construct internal hierarchies, and embed imperial nostalgia into routine spatial common sense?

**Approach:** Gavrilova conducts an inductive, grounded-theory qualitative analysis across multiple editions (2021 to 2024) of the 8th- and 9th-grade national geography textbooks (*Poliarnaya Zvezda* series) published by state-monopolized Prosveshchenie and authorized by the RGS. Drawing on critical geopolitics, Thongchai Winichakul’s concept of the national "geo-body," and postcolonial spatial theory, she unpacks discursive narratives, cartographic selections, and pedagogical prompts. The methodology traces how territorial formation, internal colonization, and regional disparity are naturalized across historical maps and visual apparatuses, especially following the 2022 full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

**Results:** The empirical analysis reveals a sophisticated machinery of territorial fabrication. First, conquest is sanitized through a lexicon of organic diffusion: the word "colonization" is excised—appearing only twice across hundreds of pages—in favor of benign terms like "resettlement," "advancement," and "economic mastering." The 2023 and 2024 editions seamlessly absorb occupied Ukrainian territories (Crimea, Donetsk, Luhansk, Kherson, and Zaporizhzhia) as "geostrategic territories with transitional regimes," accompanied by prominent callout boxes declaring that the "reunification of historical lands" began in 2014. Second, the textbooks enforce an "internal Orientalism": Moscow and Central Russia are exalted as the civilizational, dynamic core possessing innate mobility, while peripheral Siberia and the Far East are depicted merely as harsh, extraction zones (vividly underscored by maps categorizing all cultural UNESCO heritage sites in European Russia and natural sites in the East). These findings provide vital conceptual tools for decoding how modern authoritarian regimes pedagogically weaponize spatial continuity to legitimize geopolitical violence.

keyArticle.title: “Historically Russian land”. The Russian pedagogies of spatial continuity in geographical textbooks
